T: The chamber is open. So is the kitchen.
D: Harry's second year at school brings a warning from a house-elf and a monster in the walls.
P: Serve breakfast when Harry arrives at the Weasleys' house.
S: Mrs Weasley's kitchen at the Burrow
Sausages, bacon, fried eggs and buttered toast cooked all at once on a big pan, the plates loaded and passed down the table.
the pudding Dobby floats over the dinner guests

Little choux puffs baked crisp, filled with vanilla whipped cream and topped with pale violet icing and a sugared violet. Keep them on the plate. Heat the oven to 200C. Boil 125ml water, 50g butter and a pinch of salt, tip in 75g plain flour and beat over the heat for 1 minute. Cool 5 minutes, then beat in 2 eggs one at a time until glossy. Pipe 20 small mounds on lined trays and bake 20 minutes, then pierce each and bake 5 minutes more. Whip 300ml cream with 2 tbsp icing sugar and vanilla and pipe into the cooled puffs. Mix 120g icing sugar with a little water and a drop of violet colouring and spoon over.
the toffee Hagrid offers that nearly glues your teeth
Brown sugar, butter, black treacle and golden syrup boiled to 140C, poured into a tray, scored and broken once set.
M: Lamb mince browned, onion, carrot, tomato paste and Worcestershire simmered 40 minutes, topped with buttery mash, baked at 200C until golden.
Flying car beef and mushroom pies
the flying car that ends up in a tree

Beef chuck braised with mushrooms, onion and stock until tender, baked in individual shortcrust pies with flaky puff lids, with mushy peas and gravy. Brown 1kg diced chuck steak in batches. Soften 1 diced onion and 250g sliced mushrooms, return the beef, stir in 2 tbsp plain flour, 1 tbsp Worcestershire and 600ml beef stock, cover and simmer 2.5 hours until tender, then cool. Line 4 pie tins with shortcrust, fill and top with puff pastry lids. Brush with egg and bake at 200C for 30 minutes. Cook 300g frozen peas and mash roughly with butter and mint.
W: the potion brewed in the girls' bathroom
Green apple jelly set in small glasses with popping candy sprinkled on top just before serving so it fizzes.
K: a warm drink at the castle on a cold night
Brown sugar and butter cooked to a butterscotch with a splash of cream and pinch of salt, stirred into cold cream soda, topped with lightly whipped cream.

s.note: Mrs Weasley's kitchen at the Burrow
s.how: Fry 8 pork sausages until browned, then push aside and add 8 rashers of bacon and halved tomatoes. Crack in 8 eggs and fry until the whites set. Toast and butter thick slices of white bread, then load up the plates and pass them down the table.

s.note: the toffee Hagrid offers that nearly glues your teeth
s.how: Line a small tray with baking paper. Boil 200g brown sugar, 100g butter, 2 tbsp black treacle and 2 tbsp golden syrup to 140C, stirring gently. Pour into the tray, score into squares as it cools and break apart once fully set. Store in an airtight tin.

m.how: Brown 800g lamb mince, then add a diced onion and 2 grated carrots. Stir in 2 tbsp tomato paste and a splash of Worcestershire and simmer for 40 minutes. Spread in a dish, top with buttery mash from 1kg potatoes and bake at 200C until golden.

w.note: the potion brewed in the girls' bathroom
w.how: Juice 4 green apples with a squeeze of lemon and warm with 80g sugar. Soak 4 gelatine leaves, squeeze and stir in to dissolve. Pour into small glasses and chill for 4 hours. Just before serving, sprinkle popping candy on top so it crackles and fizzes.

d.note: a warm drink at the castle on a cold night
d.how: Cook 100g brown sugar with 50g butter until bubbling, then stir in a splash of cream and a pinch of salt to make butterscotch. Spoon a little into each glass, pour in cold cream soda and stir. Top with lightly whipped cream and serve in tall mugs.
